assessments.reasoning: The pinned SPDX text/MIT.txt URL supplied the claimed plain representation. Its full length and recomputed digest matched the claim. Direct comparison included the placeholders, line breaks and final LF. The same-title CRLF copy failed that test.

The pinned SPDX json/details/MIT.json body verified at 8,433 bytes with SHA-256 0c2b3c87a154a4aaac6bc6a735dd454dc29d9a78c23a85deedb080e0c65de1f8. Parsing confirmed licenseId MIT and selected licenseText. Comparing the raw escaped field contents produced a mismatch, while the decoded field reproduced the plain file.

challenge.method: Preserved the title and wording in a comparison copy while changing every LF to CRLF. Separately extracted the serialized licenseText literal from the original JSON and compared its contents, still escaped, with the plain file.
challenge.results: The CRLF copy grew to 1,096 bytes and failed equality. The escaped literal also failed equality. JSON decoding resolved the escaped newlines, quotes and angle brackets, after which the original file matched in full. Neither challenge contradicted the claim as written.

limitations: The result covers the specified SPDX revision and field with original line endings. It establishes no formal matching outcome or authority to install or redistribute a text.
